evidence.source: Shuowen.org, text of Shuowen Jiezi with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry defines 唱 as 導, ‘to lead/guide,’ and analyzes it as 从口昌聲, ‘from 口, with 昌 as phonetic.’ Duan Yucai cites the Zheng Feng line ‘唱予和女’ and says 古多以倡字爲之, that 倡 was often used for 唱 in older texts. This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of a prehistoric shape.
evidence.title: 說文解字「唱」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.text: The entry independently reports a 形聲 analysis: 口 is the semantic element and 昌 the sound element. It gives the basic sense as leading singing or music. The page displays a Small Seal form but no bronze or oracle-bone form for 唱; its displayed absence does not establish when the graph originated or that no earlier form existed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

evidence.text: The entry cites 《韓非子·解老》 for 竽唱則諸樂皆和, ‘when the yu leads, the other instruments follow’; it also cites 《文子·道原》 for the sense ‘initiate/advocate,’ 《後漢書·儒林傳上·孔僖》 for ‘praise,’ Tang Wang Bo for ‘sing,’ Tang Li He for recitation, 《北史·孫脩義傳》 for calling/shouting, and 《晉書·隱逸傳·夏統》 for a song or tune as a noun. These are cited examples, but the page does not date the individual passages or establish a complete chronology of semantic changes.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

evidence.text: For 唱, the page gives Middle Chinese category information: initial 昌, departing tone, 宕攝, 陽/漾 rhyme, open division III, and the Guangyun fanqie 尺亮. It does not provide a reconstruction of Old Chinese for 唱 on this page.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

evidence.text: The related entry 倡 is analyzed as 从人，昌聲, ‘人 plus phonetic 昌.’ It gives the Shuowen gloss 樂也, roughly ‘music/performer,’ and cites 《詩·鄭風·蘀兮》 ‘叔兮伯兮，倡予和女,’ 《禮記·樂記》 on leading a song, and further examples for singing and leading/initiating. Its analysis and examples belong to 倡 and should not be silently transferred as an earlier graphic form of 唱.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「倡」

evidence.text: The site's Old Chinese system reconstructs 昌 as tʰjaŋ and assigns it to the 陽 rhyme group. This is a system-specific reconstruction, not a directly recorded ancient pronunciation.
evidence.title: 昌 - 字 - 上古音系 - 韻典網

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstruction data
evidence.text: The entry groups 唱 with the 昌 phonetic series and gives Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *tʰjaŋ for 昌 and *tʰjaŋs for 唱. It also labels 唱 a phono-semantic compound with semantic 口 and phonetic 昌. The reconstruction offers a plausible sound relationship within that system; it is not direct evidence of the pronunciation at the graph's creation.
evidence.title: 唱 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, citing Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction
evidence.text: The Chinese-language entry reports Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese /*mə-tʰaŋ-s/ for 唱, with Middle Chinese tsyhangH and modern Beijing chàng. Its reconstruction differs in detail from Zhengzhang *tʰjaŋs; the comparison is system-dependent and should not be treated as a single consensus reconstruction.
evidence.title: 唱 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.text: The opened entry reports Standard Mandarin Pinyin chàng (fourth tone) and Cantonese Jyutping coeng3 for 唱. These modern readings differ from 昌 in tone and do not themselves establish its phonetic role; the historical comparison depends on an Old Chinese reconstruction system.
evidence.title: 唱 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry reports a proposed connection of the spoken word with 倡 and a Schuessler (2007) Sino-Tibetan comparison, including Burmese အချင်း and a tentative Proto-Bodo-Garo comparison. These are proposals about word history, not about the graphic origin of 口 or 昌; the opened entry alone does not demonstrate the comparisons or establish their chronology.
evidence.title: 唱 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The 唱 entry provides a Small Seal illustration but shows no bronze, oracle-bone, or bamboo/slip forms in its entry. No inspected source established the earliest surviving form, a sequence of graphic changes, or a corruption/reanalysis in 唱. Shuowen's component analysis is reported, but I did not visually inspect glyph images.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「唱」

search_audit.query: 說文解字 唱 導也 从口昌聲; 唱 甲骨文 金文 字形 漢語多功能字庫; 唱 上古音 昌 聲 說文 古文字; 唱 最早 用例 詩經 楚辭 漢語大詞典
search_audit.outcome: Search returned Shuowen and CUHK entries. Opened the Shuowen and 唱 pages; CUHK page reports the analysis and examples, with no ancient forms shown except Small Seal.

search_audit.query: site:ctext.org "唱予和女" 鄭風; 唱 最早 文獻 詩經 唱予和女 倡; 昌 上古音 *tʰjaŋ Zhengzhang 唱 pronunciation; 唱 上古音 Baxter Sagart 唱 昌
search_audit.outcome: Opened 韻典網's 昌 page, the Chinese Wiktionary 唱 entry, and CUHK's 倡 page. Attempts to open the Ctext passage returned internal errors. Search results distinguished 昌 and 唱 reconstructions and surfaced older 倡 spellings; no independently verified date for the cited senses was found.

gaps: No independently inspected paleographic publication or glyph image established the earliest attested graph 唱, its dated graphic evolution, or any corruption. The CUHK page shows only a Small Seal image for 唱 and no listed oracle-bone, bronze, or bamboo-slip forms.

The Shuowen gloss 導 and the cited Zheng Feng phrase support an early lexicographic understanding and an old textual example, but this research did not access a critical dated manuscript witness or establish the age of the surviving written form in that poem.

Sense citations on the CUHK entry were not independently opened in their source texts; they are recorded as that dictionary's attestations, not as primary-source verification here. The sequence from ‘lead’ to ‘sing/chant,’ ‘shout,’ and song-as-noun is therefore not claimed as a demonstrated chronology.

Old Chinese reconstructions for 昌 and 唱 vary by system. Zhengzhang gives *tʰjaŋ and *tʰjaŋs; the cited Baxter-Sagart-derived entry gives /*mə-tʰaŋ-s/ for 唱. The relation is compatible with a phonetic analysis, but needs fuller source-system comparison for detailed historical sound development.
The proposed Sino-Tibetan cognates for the spoken word are reported as a proposal only; cognacy and borrowing direction remain unverified. No whole-graph borrowing claim was substantiated.

No searched or inspected source established a distinct origin form for either 口 or 昌 as used in 唱. Their classification as separate component origins beyond their stated semantic and phonetic roles is not established.
